newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Market puzzled by large trade in FAI shares.
newsitem.headline: Market puzzled by large trade in FAI shares.

text.p: Heavy trading in shares of FAI Insurances Ltd over the past two days has the market puzzled about whether there is a takeover brewing for the company or whether the moves are merely institutions switching positions.
"There have been (takeover) rumours, but these always do the rounds from time to time," said an insurance analyst who asked not to be identified.
Added said: "Maybe some institutions have had enough and just want to sell out as (FAI shares) were looking good at one time, but now they have come back a bit and are not looking so good again."
About 23.8 million FAI shares or 7.6 percent of the insurer's issued capital traded on Tuesday.
This follows trade of 20.4 million shares on Monday, representing 6.5 percent of the group's shares.
Most of the trade was handled by Macquarie Equities, which said it could not comment on the trade.
No single shareholder on the FAI register holds anywhere near 20 million FAI shares, except for the Adler family which holds about 43 percent of the 310.5 million shares in issue.
Brokers said that if it was a potential bidder there would normally be a jump in the share price.
FAI shares closed steady at 62 cents on Tuesday.

Analysts said at these levels FAI was an attractive takeover proposition as it had a strong premium income business, but with small profitability. FAI had premium income of A$306.5 million in the six months ended December 31.
FAI shares have fallen from their record high of A$9.58 in October 1987, just before the global share market crash.
Managing director Rodney Adler was unavailable for comment on Tuesday, but on Monday he told Reuters he was unaware of who the buyer or sellers were.
